:::{#exm-central-moment-bernoulli}
#### The third central moment of a Bernoulli random variable

Let $X \sim \Ber(\prob)$,
so $\E{X} = \prob$ and $\devn(X) = X - \prob$.
The third [central moment](#def-central-moment) is:

$$
\ba
\E{[\devn(X)]^3}
&= \sum_{x \in \set{0,1}} (x - \prob)^3 \cd \P(X = x)
&& \text{(expectation of a function of a discrete random variable)} \\
&= (0 - \prob)^3 (1 - \prob) + (1 - \prob)^3 \prob
&& \text{(substitute the Bernoulli probabilities)} \\
&= \prob(1 - \prob)\paren{(1 - \prob)^2 - \prob^2}
&& \text{(factor out } \prob(1 - \prob) \text{)} \\
&= \prob(1 - \prob)(1 - 2\prob)
&& \text{(difference of squares: } (1-\prob)^2 - \prob^2 = 1 - 2\prob \text{)}
\ea
$$

For a fair coin ($\prob = 1/2$), the third central moment is $0$.
